slides.texte_overlay:
weird psychology tricks
that actually work

the nod

nod slightly while you ask someone for something. people tend to mirror small movements, and a gentle nod quietly makes saying yes feel more natural to them.

the warm drink

offer someone a warm drink before a hard conversation. studies suggest warmth in the hands makes people judge others as warmer and kinder too, so the talk goes better.

the learning effect

people listen more closely to someone who seems to know a little about everything. a few minutes of curious learning each day quietly changes how people respond to you.
slides.texte_sophia:
the learning effect

i used to stay quiet when smart topics came up. now i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app, history or science, and people really listen when i speak.

slides.texte_overlay:
the pause after

when someone gives a short answer, stay quiet for three seconds. most people fill the silence with the real answer, the one they were quietly holding back.

the name at the end

say someone's name at the end of a goodbye, not at the start of a hello. it's the last thing they hear from you, and it stays with them much longer after.
